definition: scikit-optimize does Bayesian optimisation of expensive functions, with a drop-in BayesSearchCV for scikit-learn.
details: Started in 2016 by Tim Head, Gilles Louppe, Manoj Kumar and others as a scikit-learn-adjacent project; now in maintenance mode.

explainer.lead: How to install scikit-optimize, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.
explainer.createdBy: Tim Head, Gilles Louppe and contributors.

quickstart.python:
from skopt import gp_minimize

res = gp_minimize(lambda v: (v[0] - 0.3) ** 2, [(-1.0, 1.0)], n_calls=20, random_state=0)
print(res.x, res.fun)

explainer.inAi: Tune a few expensive hyperparameters with as few training runs as possible.
explainer.jsNote: scikit-optimize is a Python library with no official JavaScript or TypeScript package; call it from a Python service if your app is written in JavaScript.

tiers.eli5: Instead of trying every combination of settings, it tries a few, learns from the results, and makes smarter guesses about where to look next.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to tune hyperparameters through BayesSearchCV inside a familiar scikit-learn workflow. A pitfall is that the project is now in maintenance mode, so new features and fixes may be limited.
tiers.paperLevel: Bayesian optimisation builds a surrogate model of the objective and selects each new evaluation point by optimising an acquisition function. Started in 2016 by Tim Head, Gilles Louppe, Manoj Kumar and others.

explainer.example: A team searching for good hyperparameters for a scikit-learn classifier swaps GridSearchCV for BayesSearchCV so that fewer training runs are needed.
